svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Tier 1 digital service — AWS reference architecture
Trust boundaries · traffic flow · failure domains · security controls · RTO 45 min · RPO 5 min · journey SLO 99.99%
Selected cloud: Amazon Web Services. Names match 01-reliability-model.md §1, the runbooks and config/.
TRUST BOUNDARY 0 — UNTRUSTED · public internet · failure domain: client
SEC: TLS 1.2+ enforced · HSTS · client retry capped at 1 (03 §3.1)
CloudWatch RUM collects real-user signal from here — canaries cannot see this hop (02 §5)
TRUST BOUNDARY 1 — AWS GLOBAL EDGE · failure domain: GLOBAL
5 regional data-plane endpoints · safety rules · readiness checks
Operable when a regional control plane is impaired
SEC: Origin Access Control — CloudFront is the only principal permitted to reach the regional origins. No direct public path to API Gateway.
Failover = two ARC routing control state changes. CloudFront, WAF, the certificate and the customer hostname never change (04 §5.2).
Edge is a global failure domain. A CloudFront or Route 53 failure is not recoverable by regional failover and is accepted as AWS-managed redundancy.
TRUST BOUNDARY 2 — REGION us-east-1 · PRIMARY (ACTIVE) · failure domain: REGION
integration timeout 4s, configured down from the 29s ceiling (03 §2.2)
per-method throttling · account quota 10,000 rps steady / 5,000 burst
SEC: Lambda authorizer validates OIDC token against locally cached JWKS.
CUJ-2 session validation makes NO runtime call to ext-idp (01 §2.1) — this is
what keeps the scored journey off the external synchronous path.
VPC — private subnets only · no public ingress to compute · security groups least-privilege
Karpenter · warm placeholder pods absorb spikes
SEC: Istio mTLS between all pods · IRSA per service
Bulkheads: separate bounded pool per dependency
ext-payments pool = 10 conns, settlement consumer ONLY
60% utilisation ceiling so 2 of 3 AZs carry full load
ADOT collector: DaemonSet agent + gateway tier (02 §2.2)
Scaling signal = in-flight requests and MSK consumer
lag via KEDA, NOT CPU. A pod blocked on a slow
dependency has low CPU and high saturation (03 §6.2).
SEC: no node has a public IP · egress via NAT only
Per-try timeout 1.5s is the SENSOR that lets the
circuit breaker detect a SLOW dependency (03 §5.2).
Envoy ejects on errors, never on latency alone.
DATA TIER — AZ-redundant within region · failure domain: REGION for the cluster, AZ for each instance
single writer — size for peak, resize = failover
alarm on oldest age, not depth
SEC: encryption at rest with multi-Region KMS keys · Secrets Manager with cross-region replica secrets · statement_timeout 1.5s on Aurora
Transactional outbox written in the SAME Aurora transaction as the transaction row, so MSK is a SOFT dependency of CUJ-4 and an MSK outage delays settlement without losing it (01 §3.1).
RPO is a MEASUREMENT, not a setting: AuroraGlobalDBRPOLag alarms at 150s, half the 5-minute objective, so action is possible before the objective is missed (04 §4.2).
Aurora Global Database — physical replication, sub-second typical
Unplanned failover: RPO = replication lag at the moment of failure. Planned switchover: zero loss (04 §4.1).
Replicates CORRUPTION too — a data fault is NOT a failover case (04 §2.2).
Consumer group OFFSET sync + identical topic names.
Offset position, not durability, is the binding RPO constraint (04 §4.5).
TRUST BOUNDARY 3 — REGION us-west-2 · RECOVERY (WARM) · failure domain: REGION
STATIC STABILITY: identical topology at FULL production capacity. Recovery does not depend on scaling up a region under stress while every other AWS customer does the same (03 §9.1).
No application configuration changes during failover. Apps address the RDS Proxy, topic names are identical, and the customer hostname never moves.
syn-cuj1..5 canaries run here CONTINUOUSLY at 1-minute frequency. Their standing green state is the evidence that this region can serve TODAY, which is the
direct answer to "DR has never been exercised end to end", and the input to the decision-tree branch that forbids failing into an unverified region (04 §2.2).
SEC: multi-Region KMS keys · replica secrets · ECR cross-region replication · service quotas matched and alarmed · ACM certs issued in BOTH regions.
ARC readiness checks continuously diff this region against the primary and surface drift BEFORE it matters (04 §5.4).
ddb-tier1-idempotency — DynamoDB Global Table · ACTIVE-ACTIVE in both regions · failure domain: MULTI-REGION
Idempotency state must survive the loss of the region whose failure makes replay necessary, so it cannot live in the Aurora cluster being recovered (03 §4.3).

ACCEPTED RISK: last-writer-wins replication leaves a lag window where a duplicate can slip through during failover. Bounded, not eliminated. Caught by reconciliation (04 §7.3) and reported, not hidden.
TRUST BOUNDARY 4 — EXTERNAL PROVIDERS · OUTSIDE ALL AWS BOUNDARIES · failure domain: THIRD PARTY, not controllable
CUJ-2 validation makes NO call here
Two providers at 99.9% on the synchronous path cap the journey at 99.79% — 21x over a 99.99% error budget (00 §2.4).
This is why submit returns 202 Accepted on a DURABLE WRITE and settles asynchronously. The arithmetic drove the architecture.
Worst failure mode is SLOW-BUT-UP, not down: it returns 200, holds connections, exhausts pools and never trips an error-based breaker (01 §4.4).
syn-ext-payments and syn-ext-idp probe from BOTH regions continuously, which is what proves the recovery region's egress is allowlisted before it is needed.
2 origin fetch via OAC → active region only

Request path: 1 client → 2 CloudFront origin fetch → 3 API Gateway private integration → 4 Aurora write + outbox in one transaction, return 202 → 5 outbox relay to MSK, consumer reads → 6 settle with provider.

Failure domains, innermost outward: pod → AZ (3 per region) → region (2) → global edge → third party. Steps 1 to 4 are the scored 99.99% journey. Steps 5 and 6 carry a separate 15-minute freshness SLO.
